question.text: In commodity futures, the settlement price used for delivery default penalty and compensation to non-defaulting parties is called the Final Settlement Price (FSP), also known as:

explanation.text: The Logic: Final Settlement Price (FSP), also called the Due Date Rate (DDR), is the rate at which the exchange settles the contract on the due date and is used for delivery default penalty and compensation to non-defaulting parties. The Trap: Base price is used for DPL. Circuit limit is the DPL itself. Reference price is a general term not specific to this purpose. The Daily Settlement Price (DSP) handles daily MTM and is a different price. Note: Keep DSP (daily MTM) and FSP/DDR (final settlement, delivery default penalty, buyer compensation) clearly separated.
